rule: Explicit combined-source interpretation: Proclamation1400/2026 Articles2(1–2,7),3 and4 confine plant import documents to living plants, pest-risk plant products and pest-capable articles deemed to require measures. Actual clean steam-manufactured sencha is inferred outside that class, using current-linked ISPM32 tea Category1 as technical evidence. Article25(2) disapplies inconsistent older breadth; Article26 preserves Regulation4/1992. Its Article3 likewise uses infestation liability and ScheduleI item11 names Camellia sinensis without specifically regulating manufactured tea. The former1971unqualified natural/dried/manufactured definition cannot automatically override the2026risk qualification. This is a legal/processing inference, with the botanical-list counterargument preserved in the peer review, not an Ethiopian commodity ruling.
personalMailApplicability: The plant scope inference applies regardless of private postal transport; no passenger/gift exemption is being borrowed. Ordinary customs and arrival inspection remain. No raw additives, pests, soil, straw or wood packaging. Independent private-food scope is being reviewed separately.
remainingQuestion: Independent private-food documentary scope under Proclamation1112/2019 and current implementing EFDA rules. The current plant-law full text has been recovered; no longer claim it is unavailable. Agricultural interpretation is proposed as conditional support and preserves the1992continuity counterargument.
researchAttempts: Located and read the new 2026 proclamation rather than carrying forward the superseded law; searched commodity schedules and personal-use exceptions.

Reconfirmed on 30 September 2026 that the Ministry of Justice lists Proclamation 1400/2026 as in force from 7 May 2026. Re-attempted the official PDF and searched current commodity schedules and exact-title mirrors; official PDF retrieval returned 403 in this follow-up. No new tea-specific implementing classification or private-post exception was established, so the earlier unresolved finding is preserved rather than falling back to the repealed 1992 law.

30 September independent food/conformity pass: Recovered actual Gazette Proclamation 1112/2019 and visually verified article 10(1), PDF page 20: food imports require safety compliance and an executive-organ permit. However article 3, PDF page 13, limits the law’s scope to products intended for market placement or otherwise offered for public use. Article2(1) defines food to include processed human-consumption substances. Regulation 531/2023 defines the agency and its powers, not a new unqualified private import duty. The current eRIS portal describes special import applications but in an importer/vendor/licensing chain; it does not settle private personal food parcels. Complete FAO-hosted Gazette law and 2023 agency regulation downloaded; article 10 visually verified because PDF OCR is poor. Ministry of Justice labels 1112/2019 in force. Personal medical/supplement exceptions and customs tax allowances were not extended to ordinary tea.

30 September legal-scope peer review: recovered the complete official English translation of Food Exporters, Importers and Wholesalers Control Directive 22/2014, hosted by USDA. Article 4 limits it to food-trade companies; article 8(1) expressly exempts personal-consumption food from the certificate of competence. Article 20(4) separately lists shipment health and origin certificates, and article 8 does not expressly waive those. This is an older directive and its present interaction with Proclamation 1112/2019 was not established. The 2025 USDA FAIRS report describes processed tea notification and commercial import documents but supplies no private-postal scope rule; its reliance on the 1992 plant regulation cannot override the new 2026 proclamation. These sources narrow the licensing issue without clearing tea or proving an unavoidable private-parcel certificate.

30 September fresh official-online recovery: Read current Ministry of Justice Coffee and Tea Authority registered-directive index, including 2026 entries. The available directive titles concern coffee marketing/quality control or spices, not an operative private tea import rule. An EFDA 2023–2026 implementation plan describes future regulatory work rather than an enacted private-food exception.

currentPrimarySource.dateNote: September media upload is not enactment.

provisions.finding: Plant means living plants/parts. Plant product means processed or natural plant-based product exposed to pest-introduction/distribution risk because of its nature or processing. The risk phrase qualifies the class; processed origin alone is insufficient.

Other regulated articles are pest-capable objects deemed to require quarantine measures. Wood packaging excludes paper products. Commodity and consignment definitions remain limited to plants, plant products and other regulated articles.

Post-harvest pests and prevention during processing/storage are recognized. These general surveillance/control provisions do not independently require an import permit for every clean manufactured food. They preserve action against actual postprocessing contamination.

Scientific/PRA basis, import permits and release authorization attach to the defined plant/plant-product/regulated-article classes. Article4(4) addresses the restricted list, rather than bringing all nonregulated manufactured products within the law. The awkward English4(2) calls its origin-related document an import permit; no silent relabelling as a phytosanitary certificate is needed for the excluded-class inference.

Wood packaging has independent treatment/logo conditions. The scenario should use clean factory retail packing and paper/cardboard/plastic outer packaging without wood, soil, straw or raw plant filler.

The authority must discharge IPPC obligations under national law; delegated measures must accord with this Proclamation and relevant international phytosanitary standards. This is operative standards context, not mere international membership, but neither clause creates automatic direct adoption of every illustrative ISPM category.

Inspectors may inspect defined goods, suspend suspect consignments, collect samples and act on regulated pests. Ordinary truthful customs declaration and arrival inspection remain. No independent all-food import duty appears here.
Repeals Decree56/1971; disapplies inconsistent laws/customary practices; expressly continues Regulation4/1992 until replacement; effective on Gazette publication7May2026.

Plants include plant products and borrow the1971definition. Article3 subjects infestation-liable goods to quarantine. Articles4/6 impose permits/phyto on ScheduleI goods. Item11 names Camellia sinensis without raw/dried/manufactured specification. It is not confined on its face to planting material; some other entries expressly exclude seeds and ScheduleIII includes consumption imports. Its research/transit waiver is not a personal exemption.
Original EAA scan visually verified: leaves and products in natural, dried or manufactured state were included without a risk qualification. That definition is materially broader than2026Article2(2).

interpretation.application: Actual industrial steaming, rolling and drying produces manufactured sencha; current-linked ISPM32 Appendix2 tea Category1 is commodity-specific technical evidence that pre-existing plant-pest risks are eliminated by processing. The appendix is illustrative/nonprescriptive and does not itself waive a domestic law. It supports applying the actual2026risk-qualified domestic definition to clean sealed tea.
interpretation.continuity: Read Articles25(2) and26 together: compatible1992requirements continue for regulated Camellia plants/products, while the former1971unqualified manufactured-product breadth cannot override the new higher-law risk definition. The saved1992Article3 already conditions quarantine on infestation liability. ScheduleI lists a species, not expressly processed or dried tea as a distinct regulated commodity. It therefore need not be treated as a contrary determination that every manufactured derivative poses risk.
interpretation.counterargument: The1992definition incorporates the old broad manufactured scope, and ScheduleI expressly names Camellia. Article26continuation is unqualified in its sentence. A contrary reading could preserve that whole species category temporarily. The proposed interpretation rejects that blanket breadth because it would nullify the new Article2risk limitation and Article25(2)inconsistency rule; the schedule still has ample compatible operation for live/raw/risk-capable Camellia. This legal-scope inference must remain plainly labelled.
interpretation.limits: ISPM32does not address storage pests or postprocessing contamination. Clean new packaging, absence of pests/raw plant additives and ordinary inspection are conditions. No personal-use quantitative exemption is asserted.
